chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik from Abdillah ibn Jabala from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In
a man who undertakes fasting as a vow and is unable to do so, he said: 'He gives two mudds to one who fasts on his behalf for each day.'

key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: Two mudds (a unit of volume for food)

ai.seo_question: What is the fidya (expiation) for a person who cannot fulfill a fasting vow due to inability?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fidya (expiation) for a vow of fasting when the vow-maker is incapacitated, prescribing two mudds of food for each day to a substitute who fasts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general fasting expiation and vow-specific obligations, emphasizing the flexibility in fulfilling religious commitments through substitution when physical ability is lacking. The measurement of two mudds reflects the prophetic tradition of charity, linking the act of fulfilling a vow to the spiritual merit of feeding the poor.
